bounded-context.name: Design system
bounded-context.purpose: The shared visual vocabulary of the viewer: design tokens (color, typography, geometry), the `lexicon-ink` Monaco theme, and the small family of reusable primitives that appear across surfaces (`RefLink`, `InlineCode`, `CodeAnchorBadge`, `PeekDrawer`, `Marginalia`). Owns the editorial-meets- blueprint aesthetic; surfaces consume from this context rather than declaring their own colors / fonts / shapes.
bounded-context.narrative:
Tokens, primitives, theme — in that order. The are the single canonical source for color, typography, and geometry; raw hex literals outside `styles/index.css` are vocabulary drift (). Every surface consumes via Tailwind utilities or `var(--color-…)`; the palette is small and load-bearing.
Above the tokens sit a small family of primitives every surface uses: for entity references, for backtick-spanning names, as the *only* entry point that opens a peek, as the Monaco host, for the right-rail metadata layout. Bypassing them (raw `<a>`, hand-rolled span splits, direct `usePeek` calls) re-implements the affordance and loses visual consistency ().
The is the Monaco theme defined once in `PeekDrawer.tsx`: vs-dark base, vellum on ink-2, oxide-tinted line decoration. Every peek inherits it. A single `PeekProvider` wraps every project surface () — switching ↔ never closes peeks or drops scroll position. The Light Table moment is the affordance the drawer carries; resetting on a toggle would defeat the point.

term.name: design tokens
term.definition: Tailwind v4 `@theme` block: `--color-ink`, `--color-ink-2/3/4`, `--color-rule`, `--color-vellum`, `--color-vellum-2/3`, `--color-oxide`, `--color-oxide-2`, `--color-saffron`; `--radius-card: 0`, `--radius-pill: 2px`; font families bound to Fraunces (display) and IBM Plex Mono (mono). Defined once in `styles/index.css`; consumed via Tailwind utility classes or `var(--color-…)` in inline styles.

term.name: RefLink
term.definition: The clickable entity-reference primitive. Renders a `<Link>` to the target entity's route with the kind glyph (`T` / `I` / `D` / `Sf` / …) in mono micro plus the display name via `InlineCode`. The 1px oxide underline visual signature for in-prose references comes from the `ref-link` CSS class.

term.name: InlineCode
term.definition: Renders an entity name whose body may contain backtick-wrapped code spans (`InlineCode text="like \`this\`"`). Spans inside backticks render in IBM Plex Mono so identifiers read as code rather than as literal words. Used everywhere a `ref.name` is shown.

term.name: CodeAnchorBadge
term.definition: Clickable badge that opens its `CodeAnchor` as a peek in the drawer. Displays the relative file path, the formatted line range, and the symbol if present. The only entry point that opens peeks — both surfaces route through it.

term.name: PeekDrawer
term.definition: The Monaco-hosting drawer that renders each open `Peek` as a small editor (`@monaco-editor/react`) with the `lexicon-ink` theme and line decorations highlighting the anchored range. Multiple peeks stack vertically. Width persisted via `usePersistedWidth`. Shared across reading-room and graph-view surfaces.

term.name: Marginalia
term.definition: Two-component pair (`<Marginalia>` + `<MarginaliaItem label=…>`) that lays out the right-rail metadata for an entity: owner (context or kernel), validation mode, disambiguatesFrom, upstream/downstream (seams), participants, code anchors, codeModules, source file. Each item is a smallcap label over a small column of content.

term.name: lexicon-ink Monaco theme
term.definition: The Monaco editor theme defined once in `PeekDrawer.tsx`'s `defineTheme`: vs-dark base, vellum text on ink-2 background, oxide-tinted line decoration. Applied to every peek. `plans/git-history/spec.md` notes a planned extraction into `lib/monaco-theme.ts` so HistoryTimeline can share it.

invariant.name: colors come from tokens, not literals
invariant.statement: Color values in component code reference `var(--color-…)` or the Tailwind utility derived from the `@theme` block. Raw hex / rgb / hsl literals outside `styles/index.css` are vocabulary drift.
invariant.rationale: The editorial palette is small and load-bearing; an inline `#b8472d` somewhere is a future-rename hazard and obscures intent. The token file is the canonical source — keep it that way so palette evolution stays a single-file edit. lex-audit flags hex literals outside `styles/index.css` per the design-system signals in lex-overview.

invariant.name: peek state persists across surfaces
invariant.statement: A single `PeekProvider` wraps every project surface (`/p/:id/*`). Switching between reading-room and graph-view does not close open peeks, drop their scroll position, or re-fetch their file contents.
invariant.rationale: The Light Table moment — "everything is at your fingertips" — is the core affordance the peek drawer carries; losing peeks on a view toggle would defeat the purpose. `plans/_archive/graph-view/spec.md` is explicit about this; any future surface added under `/p/:id/...` must mount inside the existing provider, not its own.

invariant.name: shared primitives, not raw HTML
invariant.statement: Entity refs route through `<RefLink>`, not raw `<Link>` or `<a>`. Code anchors route through `<CodeAnchorBadge>`, not direct `usePeek` calls. Names with backtick spans route through `<InlineCode>`, not hand-rolled span splits.
invariant.rationale: The primitives carry the underline, the glyph, the peek-open behavior, and the inline-code-span discipline. Bypassing them means re-implementing the affordance and losing the visual consistency that lets the viewer read as one document rather than a patchwork.
